stories.title: Bordeaux braced for heatwave as wildfire battle continues
stories.summary: France is bracing for its fourth major heatwave of the year, as soaring temperatures and tinder-dry conditions add to pressure on crews battling a giant wildfire near Bordeaux. It has now been a week since this wildfire began its destructive path through the Gironde region in south west France. Several significant flare-ups yesterday forced the precautionary evacuation of thousands more residents and holiday-makers - and there are concerns more could follow. Authorities say they have managed to stabilise the fire - despite 14 significant flareups yesterday - and several more overnight.

stories.title: Two judges criticise solicitors' withdrawal of services
stories.summary: Two High Court judges have criticised solicitors withdrawing their services, as they were forced to adjourn trials and sentencing matters involving child complainants and serious sexual offending. Mr Justice Paul McDermott was told today that a new trial date needed to be set for a sexual abuse case involving a child complainant. The court heard that the solicitor in the case withdrew their services on the original trial date in June. The child complainant is in counselling. The trial had been otherwise ready to proceed, the court heard. Mr Justice McDermott set a new trial date for the autumn term, telling the court it would have to proceed on that day.

stories.title: European fisheries ministers to meet in Cork
stories.summary: Fisheries ministers from across the EU are gathering in Cork today for a two-day informal meeting. The meeting is part of Ireland's Presidency of the Council of the EU and the plenary session will be chaired by Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine, Martin Heydon. At the plenary session in Cork City Hall tomorrow, ministers will discuss how the EU can sustainably develop its fisheries and aquaculture, as well as generational renewal in both sectors. The meeting will also be attended by the EU Commissioner for Fisheries and Oceans, Costas Kadis, and by the Vice-Chair of the European Parliament Fisheries Committee, Paulo Do Nascimento Cabral, as well as by delegations from across EU member states.

stories.title: Ahead of sale, PTSB says on track for full year targets
stories.summary: PTSB has reported higher half year profits and income and said it remains on track to deliver its financial targets for the full year. The bank said its underlying profit before tax for the six months to the end of June rose by 34% to €68m, while its total income for the period grew by 7% to €344m. PTSB said its total gross loans increased by 4% to €22.9 billion, while total lending was up 6% to €1.7 billion. The lender reported new mortgage lending of 1.3% for the first half of the year, which gave it a market share of about 19%.

stories.title: Oman presents plan for Strait of Hormuz fees to Iran
stories.summary: Oman has presented Iran with a plan backed by Gulf states to manage the Strait of Hormuz, including collecting voluntary fees for using it, a Gulf source and a Western diplomat have told Reuters. The plan could serve as a basis to end the disruption to trade through the strait caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran. President Donald Trump, who abruptly called off a two-week US. bombing campaign over the weekend in his latest strategic U-turn, said there were "good talks" under way with Iran but threatened to restart strikes unless negotiations deliver. Iran denies seeking to resume talks with the United States. Washington launched its renewed bombing campaign earlier this month to break Iran's grip on the strait, through which about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flowed before the war.

Rank outsiders following their comprehensive defeat to Roscommon in the Connacht semi-final, Andy Moran, in his first season at the helm, steadied the ship and led an incredible turnaround that led to an unprecedented outpouring of emotion in Croke Park on Sunday, and right around the county. Sheehan, a Limerick native based in Nenagh, linked up with Mayo this season after previously working with the Dublin and Galway hurlers.

Infantino's social media post had advised those "spending their time and energy hating us" to "meditate, pray, or watch a football match", drawing a scathing response from Tebas. "Gianni Infantino has written a pathetic message on his Instagram account and on the accounts of @FIFAcom," Tebas (below) wrote on his own X account.

stories.title: Lowe signs for Japan club Tokyo Suntory Sungoliath
stories.summary: Former Leinster and Ireland winger James Lowe has signed for Japanese franchise Tokyo Suntory Sungoliath. Lowe, who won 45 caps for Ireland during his spell in the country, departed Irish rugby off the back of a very public and drawnout contract saga with Leinster. He amassed 102 caps for the province, playing a starring role in their 2018 EPCR Champions Cup win, as well as this season's BKT United Rugby Championship. Now he's headed for pastures new. The New Zealand-born winger will link up with the likes of former All Blacks captain Sam Cane and Toulouse scrum-half Naoto Saito upon arrival at Tokyo Suntory Sungoliath.

stories.title: Japan quake toll reaches 13 as rescue efforts continue
stories.summary: A 7.1-magnitude earthquake killed at least 13 people near the southern Japanese city of Kumamoto, and rescuers are frantically searching for survivors trapped beneath the rubble, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said. "Even now, there are people waiting to be rescued, and this is a race against time. We will marshal all available resources on the ground to save and rescue as many people as possible," Ms Takaichi told reporters at her office in Tokyo a day after the quake struck, raising the toll from three deaths reported earlier. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes and ruptured roads across the region. Eight people were pulled from the rubble of a partially collapsed shopping mall near the city of Kumamoto that was torn apart by an apparent explosion about an hour after earthquake, among them two dead women in their 20s.

Asked about that proposal, Mr Martin said that a "more independent assessment" would be appropriate in a process overseen by the European Commission rather than the company itself. "For us, it would be for the Commission, in my view, to potentially commission that type of independent assessment as well. The company is quite entitled, of course, to do that, but a more independent assessment would be, I think, an additional factor."

stories.summary: Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris has spoken with the newly appointed Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey. Mr Harris and the British Chancellor discussed a range of issues including the Ireland-UK economic and trading relationship, Ireland's EU Presidency priorities, EU-UK relations, and ongoing engagement between his Department and His Majesty’s Treasury.

stories.title: Kerry's half year revenues dip 3.7% as it updates targets
stories.summary: Food technology and ingredients company Kerry Group has reported lower revenues and after tax profits for the six months to the end of June as it announced updated financial targets up to 2030. Kerry said its revenue fell by 3.7% to €3.336 billion from €3.463 billion the same time last year, while its profit after tax fell to €282.6 from €302.8m. The company announced an interim dividend per share increase of 10% to 46.2 cent. Kerry today updated its 2030 financial targets with 3-5% annual volume growth, which it said was based on confidence in its ability to continue outperforming food and beverage end markets.

stories.summary: The man blamed for the deadly attack near Berlin's Pride parade pledged allegiance to the Islamic State group in a video, German media has said. The video was found on the phone of 21-year-old Abdul Rahman Ballout and was recorded on the day of the attack, the daily Bild cited unnamed security sources as saying. Bild reported that Ballout's phone was found inside the rented minivan the attacker ploughed into a crowd just hundreds of metres from the parade, before he crashed it into a tree in the Tiergarten park. Alongside the phone was a sheath for the machete he is believed to have used to attack more people after leaving the vehicle.

Before kick-off the Hoops introduced new signing Will Fitzgerald, the now former Sligo Rovers captain who moved Tallaght for a fee believed to be in the region of €75,000.

However, Tehran ruled out Oman's proposal for regional joint management of the strait, saying it had no chance of success, a senior Iranian official said. The US and Saudi Arabia are trying to pressure Oman to advance their "unrealistic plans" regarding the strategic strait, the official said.

stories.summary: Apple's market capitalisation briefly surpassed $5 trillion for the first time yesterday, making it only the second company ever to achieve that milestone after Nvidia. At a session high of $342.89 on Wall Street last night, Apple's market value stood at $5.036 trillion. Apple became the most valuable company in the world earlier this month, overtaking chipmaker Nvidia - which had been at the top since June 2025 and was the first company ever to breach the $5 trillion threshold. Nvidia's shares were last up 0.53% at $197.63, valuing it at $4.78 trillion.

stories.title: Catholic pilgrimage site of Medjugorje desecrated
stories.summary: A popular Catholic pilgrimage site in Bosnia has been vandalised and a nearby altar set ablaze, authorities said, days before tens of thousands are expected to gather at the shrine. The Marian shrine of Medjugorje, about 140km southwest of the capital Sarajevo, rose to fame in the 1980s after purported apparitions of the Virgin Mary there. It has become one of the most popular pilgrimage sites, with more than one million people visiting every year. Local media published images of the damage, showing black spray paint covering the central statue of the Virgin Mary's face and the words "devil in a skirt" on its pedestal.

stories.title: Treacy: Bohs have enough to edge past 'beatable' Ballkani
stories.summary: Keith Treacy believes Bohemians have enough in the tank to hold onto their narrow first leg advantage over Ballkani on Thursday and advance to the third qualifying round of the Conference League. During last week's first leg, Alan Reynolds' side showed resolve in bouncing back from a first-half concession to win 2-1 in the last European game at Dalymount Park in its current guise. The highlight of the evening last Wednesday was Ross Tierney's spectacular late winner which sets up a nervy away leg against their Kosovan opponents who have European pedigree from recent seasons. While Bohs' advantage is narrow, former Republic of Ireland winger Treacy is optimistic that the north Dublin side can go to the Kosovan capital Pristina and see the tie through.
